# Related Work {#sec-related-work}

Organized by the composition claim itself: five clusters, each already
attested in the literature, none composed with the others into the form
this paper states. Each cluster closes with the line that distinguishes
this paper's use of it from the source's own.

## (a) The residue thesis, stated repeatedly, never factored

The thesis that trust occupies exactly the space verification cannot
reach is old. For Frankel, trust takes the place of an assessment that
cannot easily be made, or is too costly to attempt; it enters "where
more exact knowledge is not available" [@frankel-1977]. The Lewis and
Weigert formulation — trust "begins where prediction ends"
[@lewis-weigert-1985] — reaches this paper through Möllering's
genealogy, where the tradition's unfactored form is plainest: trust as a
leap "across the gorge of the unknowable" that "brackets out uncertainty
and ignorance" as one undifferentiated act [@mollering-2001]. Later work
inherits it intact — an attitude that lowers "the barrier of monitoring,
challenging, checking, and questioning" [@nguyen-unquestioning].
Security-requirements engineering operationalizes the same residue as a
discretionary argument-stopper: "trust assumptions are unsubstantiated
grounds used in security satisfaction arguments... because trust
assumptions are not argued, they stop the grounds-to-claim recursion"
[@haley-et-al-2005]. Formal e-voting verifiability gives the strongest
formal near-miss: the residue is named explicitly and the inference from
"unverifiable" to "trusted" is stated outright, but the residue itself
is a concrete, per-protocol component list, never factored by cause
[@kremer-ryan-smyth-2010]. That treatment is field-standard rather than
idiosyncratic: the systematization of verifiability notions across
e-voting finds the residue carved throughout by *honest-principal sets* —
who must behave — and never by the cause of the failure
[@cortier-et-al-2016]. The requirements lineage reaches 2024 with the
gap still open, in a theory of security-related assumptions built
directly on the trust-assumption tradition above, where decidability,
monotonicity, and verifiability limits do not appear at all
[@corallo-et-al-2024].

Trust taxonomies come nearest to naming a structure and stop short.
One decomposes trust in secure systems into seven attributes across six
dimensions, but every dimension is a property of the *measurement
apparatus* — how confidently, how recently, on whose authority an
attribute was assessed — rather than an axis along which a claim can
fail. Its bottom rung, "Assumed," is a single flat bucket with no
account of why an attribute lands there; its closest approach to a limit
result is an explicitly informal remark on bootstrapping circularity
[@bradbury-et-al-2022].

**Line:** the thesis is old, repeatedly operationalized down to the
level of individual security arguments and protocol analyses, and still
current in 2024. The residue is never factored *by cause* in any of
these sources.

## (b) The mathematical home of two axes

Certifiability and monotonicity, taken together as one bundled notion —
a semi-decidable property that is also stable under extension — is
exactly the algebra of *observable* (or *affirmable*) properties in
synthetic topology and domain theory, established decades before this
paper: priority to Smyth's topological treatment of predicate
transformers [@smyth-1983], developed by Abramsky's logic of observable
properties [@abramsky-1987], consolidated by Vickers [@vickers-1989],
and given its effective, computable form by Escardó, whose dictionary —
semi-decidable property corresponds to open set, "observable" and
"affirmable" name the same thing — is the form this paper actually
instantiates [@escardo-2004]. That algebra's arrival in security is
already documented: protocol-analysis goals are formalized as geometric
sentences — exactly the finite-meet, arbitrary-join fragment of this
algebra — with the trust policy itself held outside the algebra, as raw
input never run through it [@dougherty-guttman-ramsdell-2018].

**Line:** both axes are inherited and credited. This paper's delta is
the *snapshot/enduring factoring* of the classical bundle
(@sec-factorization) and the identification of the residue with trust,
neither of which these sources perform. That the algebra reached
security at all is not this paper's finding — it is already documented
above, which is why no such claim is made anywhere in this paper.

## (c) The determination anchors

That authenticity is not recoverable from a document's intrinsic form
alone was hypothesized and *tested*, not merely asserted: the
InterPARES Authenticity Task Force set out to show that intrinsic and
extrinsic elements of documentary form establish authenticity, across
case studies, and reported the hypothesis unsupported — "context shifts
the analysis away from the record itself to the broader structural,
procedural, and documentary framework" [@interpares-2002]. That finding
has already crossed into computer science once, explicitly imported
[@factor-et-al-2009]. The philosophical anchor for the determination
axis more generally is Goodman's autographic/allographic distinction
[@goodman-1968]. A cluster of design axioms in modern
software-supply-chain security is built entirely around the same
premise without ever stating it as a limit: provenance and attestation
frameworks exist precisely because genuineness is not recoverable from
an artifact's bytes alone [@slsa; @in-toto; @c2pa; @prov-dm; @rfc9334].

**Line:** the determination axis is reasoned about, tested, and
engineered around — but never formalized as a decision-procedure-level
limit over a byte string. That formalization is this paper's own.

## (d) The monotonicity iff

Monotonicity's identification with coordination-freedom is a
biconditional in its own right, refereed for relational transducers
[@ameloot-neven-vandenbussche-2013] and generalized, in an unrefereed but
version-pinned preprint, to arbitrary concurrent specifications
[@hellerstein-2026]. That work's own use of a Rice-theorem-flavored
remark is worth noting precisely because of how it differs from this
paper's use: it applies decidability *to* monotonicity, as a remark
about the cost of *checking* whether a specification is monotone, never
*beside* monotonicity as a co-equal axis of a trust taxonomy.

**Line:** the biconditional is inherited from CALM; this paper's axis is
the *evidence-endurance* reading of monotonicity specifically, composed
alongside determination and certifiability rather than studied alone.

## (e) Bounding the residue, rather than reducing or reaching it

Two prior lines address "how much must be trusted," and neither
characterizes or bounds a residue the way this paper does. Gligor and
Woo prove a trusted state *reachable*, unconditionally, from an
untrusted starting point — a positive construction that makes *how small
can the trusted remainder be?* well-posed without answering it
[@gligor-woo-2019]; this paper's verification ceiling (@sec-instances)
is that answer. The self-maintaining compiler trapdoor was described,
and costed, in the 1974 security evaluation of Multics: a trapdoor
placed in the PL/I compiler that reinstates itself on every rebuild.
"Since the PL/I compiler is itself written in PL/I, the trap door can
maintain itself, even when the compiler is recompiled"
[@karger-schell-1974]. Thompson named the problem ten years later and
is the reason the field knows it [@thompson-1984]. The lineage
descending from it *reduces or diversifies* the trusted base without
ever proving a residual base *minimal*. Diverse double-compiling is its
sharpest instance — rebuild with an independent compiler and compare —
and Wheeler enumerates what the technique still requires: a trusted
compilation process, a trusted comparer, trusted environments, and a
trusted way to obtain both the compiler under test and its source
[@wheeler-2005]. A smaller trusted base, and nowhere an argued-minimal
one.
Durán and Formanek give the closest genuine
decomposition of a verification barrier this sweep found, into two
agent-relative conditions, accessibility and surveyability — but with no
computability-theoretic content, and a framing that treats epistemic
opacity as a property of a cognitive agent's access rather than of a
decision procedure over a bit string [@duran-formanek-2018].

**Line:** this paper's contribution is a negative, characterize-and-bound
result where the lineage offers positive constructions (reachability) or
unbounded reduction (diversify the compiler, shrink the TCB) — the
residue is bounded and proved minimal, not merely made smaller.

## The pattern

| Ingredient | Attested? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Determination | yes — reasoned and empirically tested | Goodman 1968; InterPARES ~2002 (hypothesis falsified); Factor et al. 2009 (carried into CS) |
| Certifiability $\times$ monotonicity, as one bundled algebra | yes — since 1983 | Smyth 1983; Abramsky 1987; Vickers 1989; Escardó 2004 |
| Monotonicity $\Leftrightarrow$ coordination-freedom | yes — as an iff | Ameloot–Neven–Van den Bussche 2013; Hellerstein 2026 |
| Trust as the residue of verification | yes — as a thesis, repeatedly, through 2024 | Frankel 1977; Lewis & Weigert 1985; Möllering 2001; Nguyen; operationalized by Haley et al., Kremer–Ryan–Smyth, Cortier et al. 2016, Corallo et al. 2024 |
| **The composition of all four** | **not found in any venue reached** | — |

Every ingredient has a home; the composition has none this sweep could
reach. A further pattern corroborates that absence rather than merely
restating it. Across three unrelated subfields — root-of-trust
establishment, protocol analysis, e-voting verifiability — the
literature consistently formalizes what must be *established* and
consistently declines to formalize what must be *assumed*
[@gligor-woo-2019; @dougherty-guttman-ramsdell-2018;
@kremer-ryan-smyth-2010]. That is not plausibly one community's
stylistic accident, and it is an argument from positive evidence about
what the field *did* do, which does not depend on the coverage limits
of @sec-scope-objections.
